name: Bean & Bloom Café
tagline: A tiny neighborhood café: perfect for your very first queries.
description: Bean & Bloom is a cosy café with a short menu, a handful of regulars and a few months of orders. The tables are small enough to read at a glance, so it is the ideal place to learn SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and your first JOIN. Some values are missing on purpose (emails, calories, tips) so you can meet NULL early.

name: ShopSmart
tagline: An online store with customers, orders, payments and reviews.
description: ShopSmart is a small online store with two years of orders, 60 products, 150 customers and their payments and reviews. It is the main playground for joins, GROUP BY, subqueries and CTEs, with realistic quirks like customers who never ordered and orders that are not paid yet. Dates run from January 2023 to December 2024, with busy Black Friday seasons.

name: Acme Corp
tagline: Departments, employees, managers, salaries and projects.
description: Acme Corp is a mid-sized company with 55 employees spread across seven departments and a five-level management chain from the CEO down to individual contributors. Use it to learn self joins, recursive CTEs and window functions such as RANK() over salaries, and to practice finding departments without people. It also has a full salary history and a handful of projects with assignments.

name: FitTrack
tagline: Product analytics for a fitness app: events, funnels, retention and streaks.
description: FitTrack is a fitness app with 300 users, about 7,000 tracked events, subscriptions and a table of daily step counts. It is built for product analytics: funnels, weekly retention by signup cohort, sessionization, streaks (gaps and islands) and reading JSON properties. Events come in bursts (sessions) separated by hours or days of silence.

name: Messy Data Co.
tagline: Dirty, real-world data: clean it with TRIM, LOWER, CASE, CAST and more.
description: Messy Data Co. exports its data from old systems, so everything arrives as text: names in odd cases, phone numbers in many formats, dates written five different ways and duplicates hiding in plain sight. Use it to practice cleaning with TRIM, LOWER, REPLACE, CASE, COALESCE, NULLIF and CAST, finding duplicates, and reshaping data with pivot and unpivot. Nothing here is secret or personal: all names and emails are made up.
